messages:
maria: FYI AcmeCorp reporting intermittent 429s from their Dedicated pool (dedicated-gold-2). Started ~08:13 UTC after we rolled a routeset policy change earlier today. They see bursts every 10-30s, only for tenant acme-prod.

acme-support: [from customer] We see tokens failing with 429 even though dashboard shows available capacity. Example request id: req_8f3a9b - headers attached below.

maria: proxy log snippet:
```
[08:13:12] req=req_8f3a9b status=429 route=none pool=dedicated-gold-2 decision_trace=trace-20260317-01
[08:13:22] req=req_8f3a9c status=429 route=none pool=dedicated-gold-2 decision_trace=trace-20260317-01
```
controlplane trace id: trace-20260317-01
headers pasted by customer:
```
X-Redwood-Routeset: premium,priority=5
X-Redwood-Tier: gold
X-Redwood-Tenant: acme-prod
```
Customer note: they edited the routeset in the UI and used a comma to separate attributes.

devin: Are the 429s emitted at the gateway layer or after controlplane route decision? Can you attach the full controlplane decision capture for trace-20260317-01 and the proxy log lines around it? Also any recent controlplane deploys?

maria: attaching decision dump excerpt (paste below). Decision shows fallback to coldpool and throttle cap applied, even though pool assignment should have matched dedicated-gold-2.

leo: Quick read: routeset parser change in v2.2.0 changed attribute tokenization. Previously attributes were key/value pairs joined by semicolons; v2.2.0 introduced a CSV-style split for backwards compat but incorrectly treats ",priority=5" as a standalone routeset item rather than an attribute on 'premium'. That leads to no matching tier -> fallback -> throttle.

jordan: Confirmed on the decision dump: matched_routeset=["premium","priority=5"] -> match logic tried to find a routeset named 'priority=5' -> miss -> fallback to default coldpool -> throttle caps.

devin: Immediate mitigations: 1) ask customer to send X-Redwood-Routeset with semicolon: `premium;priority=5` or 2) set explicit header X-Redwood-Pool: dedicated-gold-2. I've also applied a temporary quota bump for tenant acme-prod to avoid customer impact while we fix the parser.

maria: Applied workaround and instructed customer. They retried and report healthy responses. Customer: "requests back to normal, no 429s for 5 minutes."

deploy-bot: Rolled back controlplane/routeset-parser from v2.2.0 -> v2.1.8 (08:20 UTC) :white_check_mark:

leo: Root cause summary: ambiguous delimiter handling in routeset grammar caused attribute tokens to be treated as separate routeset items. Fix plan: revert parser change (done), add strict parsing and validation in config UI, add unit tests for comma vs semicolon cases, and add a controlplane alert when >1% of requests hit fallback pool for a tenant.

maria: Filing escalation ticket (ESC-2026-043) with SRE and PM. Notified customer and offered credits for impact window. Will follow up with postmortem and timeline.

devin: Action items: (1) add regression test + CI check, (2) add config validation error on upload, (3) sRE to create alert rule for fallback-surges.

maria: Thanks all — customer unblocked and workaround + rollback in place. Closing this thread pending postmortem doc.
